UPDATES 

& 

REMINDERS IMPORTANT UPDATES & REMINDERS

summary:
**Morning drop-off begins at 8:50 AM.** Students should exit on the **passenger (right) side only** onto the front sidewalk and leave quickly to keep the line moving. 

**For afternoon pickup**, students need **one car tag with their pickup number** on the visor. Parents should stay in their cars—if the main (red) line is full, use the overflow upper lot (blue line). title: Student Cell Phone Policy and Compliance
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: Student Cell Phone Usage: Based on compliance with Senate Bill 158 Ohio Senate Bill 158 seeks to promote a focused, respectful learning environment free from personal cell phone distractions during the entirety of the school day.ExpectationsAll student cell phones must be powered off from arrival until dismissal.Phones may be stored in a student backpack and/or cubby and may not be used in classrooms, hallways, restrooms, recess, or the cafeteria at any time during the school day.Additional electronic devices that allow communication or internet use may also be stored should they present a disruption.Consequences for Cell Phone Violations1st Offense - students will receive a warning2nd Offense - phone confiscated & turned into office until the end of the day3rd -Offense - above procedures and the cell phone must be picked up in the office by the parent/guardianSubsequent offenses - progressive discipline, including but not limited to: loss of recess and/or privilegesAll parent/guardian contact must go through the main office. Students are never without access to communication. The school can always connect a student with a guardian using the office phone.School-Wide EmergenciesStudent safety comes first. We will not send students to hallways during an active emergency. Communication with families will be handled centrally by administration, SRO, or district personnel. If students need to access their phones after an emergency to contact family, they will be given permission and time to do so once it is safe. In some situations (e.g., prolonged shelter-in-place or reunification), supervised phone retrieval will be allowed once the situation is stable.Please note, students refusing to comply with an adult’s request to turn their phone in are subject to additional consequences.

summary: **Cell phones must be powered off and stored all day** from arrival to dismissal per Ohio Senate Bill 158. Phones cannot be used in classrooms, hallways, restrooms, recess, or cafeteria. **Violations result in progressive consequences**: 1st offense = warning, 2nd = confiscation until end of day, 3rd = parent pickup required, subsequent = loss of privileges. During school-wide emergencies, students will be given supervised access to phones once safe. All parent contact must go through the main office.

title: Community BINGO for Older Americans Month
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content:
AROUND 

THE 

COMMUNITY  AROUND THE COMMUNITY

Every May, Older Americans Month recognizes the contributions of older adults, highlights aging trends, and reaffirms commitments to serve our older community members. The 2026 theme is “Champion Your Health”.Throughout the month of May, Oxford Seniors, Age-Friendly Oxford, and the Coalition for a Healthy Community, Oxford Area are partnering to highlight and offer programming focused on promoting physical, mental, and emotional health and well-being at all ages.You can participate by playing “Community BINGO” with us! It’s as easy as 1, 2, 3!1) Print your own or pick up a Community Bingo card at any of the following locations:Oxford Seniors, 922 Tollgate Dr., OxfordOxford Lane Library, 441 S. Locust St.The Knolls of Oxford, Clubhouse or Front DeskScripps Gerontology Center, 396 Upham Hall, on campus2) Every time you do something listed on the card, mark it off. The goal is to get “BINGO” as many times as possible. A “BINGO” is marking off any 5 squares in a straight line – either vertically, horizontally, or diagonally.3) Bring your completed BINGO card to the Intergenerational BINGO Party on Sun. May 31 from 3:00 – 5:00 p.m. at Oxford Seniors for prizes, snacks, and FUN! A PDF version of the BINGO card is attached to this message if you'd like to print one at home.

title: Older Americans Month Community BINGO Challenge
source_title: Marshall E-News | Smore Newsletters for Education

blocks.content: Every May, Older Americans Month recognizes the contributions of older adults, highlights aging trends, and reaffirms commitments to serve our older community members. The 2026 theme is “Champion Your Health”.Throughout the month of May, Oxford Seniors, Age-Friendly Oxford, and the Coalition for a Healthy Community, Oxford Area are partnering to highlight and offer programming focused on promoting physical, mental, and emotional health and well-being at all ages.You can participate by playing “Community BINGO” with us! It’s as easy as 1, 2, 3!1) Print your own or pick up a Community Bingo card at any of the following locations:Oxford Seniors, 922 Tollgate Dr., OxfordOxford Lane Library, 441 S. Locust St.The Knolls of Oxford, Clubhouse or Front DeskScripps Gerontology Center, 396 Upham Hall, on campus2) Every time you do something listed on the card, mark it off. The goal is to get “BINGO” as many times as possible. A “BINGO” is marking off any 5 squares in a straight line – either vertically, horizontally, or diagonally.3) Bring your completed BINGO card to the Intergenerational BINGO Party on Sun. May 31 from 3:00 – 5:00 p.m. at Oxford Seniors for prizes, snacks, and FUN! A PDF version of the BINGO card is attached to this message if you'd like to print one at home.
